scenes.label: Meet the team
scenes.title: A useful brief
scenes.caption: The team wants a helper for festival volunteers sorting clean practice samples. Before collecting examples, Asha asks who will use it, what decision it supports and how anyone will know whether it helps.
scenes.dialogue: Useful for whom, and for which decision?

scenes.label: The problem
scenes.title: The vague promise
scenes.caption: The draft says the helper will solve all waste problems perfectly. It gives no input, output or measurable test. A broad promise leaves the team unable to decide what to build or when a person should take over.
scenes.dialogue: Perfect is not a test plan.

scenes.label: How it works
scenes.title: Make success observable
scenes.caption: Define the user, input and output. Set a measurable criterion using a fixed set of unseen examples, and specify the action for uncertainty. This is a low-stakes classroom prototype, not an autonomous system handling real waste.
scenes.dialogue: A clear limit belongs in the brief.

scenes.label: Your decision
scenes.title: Keep a human role
scenes.caption: The prototype receives a damaged or unfamiliar sample. Its training examples do not cover that condition. Should it force a label, or flag the sample for a person to review?
scenes.dialogue: Make the uncertain case part of the design.

scenes.label: What changes
scenes.title: A testable task
scenes.caption: Asha writes a brief for volunteers: suggest a practice material label from a supplied image, or request review. The team will check a fixed held-out pack and record errors. A person stays responsible for unfamiliar cases.
scenes.dialogue: Now we can tell whether the prototype meets its brief.

scenes.label: Enter the lab
scenes.title: Enter the lab
scenes.caption: Build the brief, map human review points and turn a vague goal into an acceptance criterion. The lab checks your structured decisions; your teacher can ask you to explain why those limits fit the stated task.
scenes.dialogue: Define success before looking at results.
